title: Audit and justify all golden normalization beyond time fields
description:
The current golden helpers strip and normalize substantially more than wall-clock timestamps or durations, and that policy is not documented in one place. The immediate symptom is prompt fixtures containing `"choice": "_"`, but the larger problem is that the test harness is rewriting multiple classes of data before comparison without an explicit repo-level argument for why each rewrite is acceptable.

Current behavior in `puppeteer/tests/golden_helpers.py`:
- Prompt goldens: `_normalize_prompt_for_golden()` rewrites any short ID under `id` or `choice` (for example `p11` or `l5`) to `_`.
- Prompt goldens: the same helper parses embedded JSON strings and re-serializes them with sorted keys.
- Export goldens: `_strip_volatile()` removes top-level `timestamp`, top-level `id`, top-level `errors`, per-player `thinkingTimeSecs`, per-action `ts`, per-`llmEvents` `ts`, per-`llmEvents` `latencyMs`, and per-`llmTrace` `ts`.
- Export goldens: `_strip_volatile()` also sorts `llmEvents` and `llmTrace` by `(seq, player)` instead of preserving original emission order.
- Export goldens: `_normalize_embedded_json()` rewrites HTML `object_id='UUID'` attributes to `_` and rewrites the trailing short object suffix notation like `[7e2]` to `[_]` inside strings before re-parsing nested JSON and sorting keys.

The repo currently has tests proving these rewrites are intentional (`puppeteer/tests/test_golden_helpers_normalization.py`), but not a clear statement of policy for which normalizations are allowed and which ones are too destructive.

Follow-up scope:
- Document every field/value/category that is currently stripped, rewritten, or re-ordered in golden prompt/export comparisons, with code references.
- For each normalization, explain whether it is truly unavoidable nondeterminism or whether it is hiding a real behavior difference that the golden ought to keep.
- Re-evaluate the current policy with a much stricter bar: expect pushback on stripping anything that is not literally a timestamp, latency, or similar wall-clock duration field.
- In particular, justify or remove the short-ID-to-underscore rewrite for prompt `id`/`choice`, the removal of top-level export `id`, the dropping of `errors`, the HTML object-id rewriting, and any event reordering that is not provably nondeterministic noise.
- If the final answer is that some non-time normalization must stay, document the rationale next to the helper and in the golden-test docs/skill so reviewers are not surprised by placeholders like `_` in fixtures.

The goal is to make golden tests maximally literal. If a field is not time noise, the default stance should be to keep it in the fixture unless there is a concrete, defensible reason not to.
